L1448@P42: Mass quantities for materials (AWR for all Z) and “heavy” reaction products (AWP for
L1449@P42: Z > 2) should be expressed in atomic units, i.e., the mass of the electrons should be
L1450@P42: included. Mass quantities for incident particles (AWI) and “light” reaction products (AWP
L1451@P42: for Z ≤ 2) should be expressed in nuclear mass units. For neutrons, this ratio is 1.00000.

L4686@P123: gives the threshold. If there is no threshold, use the most positive Q value of the component

L4689@P123: For the calculation of QM and QI, one must use atomic masses instead of nuclear masses
L4690@P123: for all particles with a nucleus, include light particles. For QM all atomic masses correspond
L4691@P123: to nuclei in their ground states. For QI, atomic masses correspond to nuclei in their respective
L4692@P123: nuclear excited states (i.e., the mass of the nuclear excited states are included in QI but
L4693@P123: not QM). That is QI - QM = ELIS - Ex where ELIS is the energy of the target nucleus
L4694@P123: (given in MF=1, MT=451) and Ex is the excitation energy of the residual nucleus. We use
L4695@P123: atomic rather than nuclear masses to ensure that the electron number is conserved, avoiding
L4696@P123: possible energy errors of multiples of the electron rest mass.
L4697@P123: As an example to clarify the use of QM and QI, consider the reaction α +9Be → n+X.
